summary: Turkmenistan runs one of the world's most restrictive entry regimes: virtually every nationality needs an embassy visa backed by a letter of invitation approved by the State Migration Service, normally arranged through a licensed Turkmen tour operator. There is no visa-free tourist entry.

defaultSource.name: State Migration Service of Turkmenistan — Visa ("foreign citizens enter Turkmenistan on visas unless an international treaty provides otherwise")

fee.notes: State Migration Service fee for a single-entry visa of up to one month; USD 20 for up to 10 days, USD 30 for up to 20 days, USD 30 for each further month. Multiple-entry: USD 60 for up to one month, USD 40 each further month. Children under 7 pay nothing, children 7–16 pay half; urgent processing within 3 working days doubles the fee. An invitation letter approved by the State Migration Service, arranged through a licensed tour operator, is required first.

source.name: State Migration Service of Turkmenistan — Visa fees (Wiza tölegleri)

visaTypes.name: Visa on arrival with pre-approved invitation

fee.notes: For a stay of up to one month: the USD 40 visa fee plus the USD 50 charged on every visa obtained at the international airport (USD 70 for up to 10 days, USD 80 for up to 20 days). Only for travellers whose invitation letter has already been approved by the State Migration Service.

source.name: State Migration Service of Turkmenistan — Visa fees (Wiza tölegleri)

fee.notes: Single-entry transit visa for up to 5 days; USD 40 for a double-entry transit visa of up to 5 days per trip. A letter of invitation, sponsored by the State Migration Service, is still needed first, and you must use the border crossings named on it.

source.name: State Migration Service of Turkmenistan — Visa fees (Wiza tölegleri)

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months after the date you plan to leave Turkmenistan.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Turkmenistan entry requirements

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for Turkmenistan. The UK Foreign Office advises making sure you have adequate travel health insurance and accessible funds to cover the cost of any medical treatment abroad and repatriation.

source.name: UK FCDO — Turkmenistan travel advice: health

onwardTicket.text: No official source states a return-ticket requirement. Every visa needs a letter of invitation from a sponsor (an authorised travel agency for tourists), and transit-visa holders must enter and leave through the border crossings named on the letter of invitation.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Turkmenistan travel advice: entry requirements

proofOfFunds.text: No official source we could read states a proof-of-funds requirement or amount for Turkmenistan.

declarations.name: Migration fee and registration

fee.notes: Paid on arrival. A tourism tax of USD 2 per day of stay is charged separately, usually on the hotel bill; bring US dollars in cash for any other charges at entry.

declarations.text: All foreign visitors pay a USD 14 migration fee on arrival, plus a tourism tax of USD 2 for each day of their stay. Stays of more than 3 working days must be registered with the State Migration Service within 3 days of arrival; your hotel or sponsor usually does this.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Turkmenistan entry requirements

currencyLimits.text: Foreign cash may be brought in without limit if it is declared to customs. On departure you may take out up to USD 10,000 (or the equivalent), plus any foreign currency you brought in and declared, on presenting your import declaration.

source.name: State Customs Service of Turkmenistan — For individuals: import and export of foreign currency

notes: Exporting carpets, antiques and artworks requires an expert certificate from the Ministry of Culture. Buy from licensed shops that provide the paperwork.
Strong painkillers and psychotropic medicines need supporting medical documentation; quantities are checked.

payments.text: Foreign bank cards are close to useless — acceptance is minimal and ATMs rarely work with international cards. Bring crisp US dollar notes for the whole trip and change small amounts of manat as needed.

safety.text: The crime rate is low, so take the same precautions you would at home. Land border crossings can close without notice, and access to areas near the borders with Afghanistan and Iran is tightly restricted. Although Turkmenistan has no recent history of terrorism, attacks cannot be ruled out.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Turkmenistan travel advice (safety and security)

bestTimeToVisit.text: April–May and September–October avoid the extreme Karakum desert heat — pleasant for Ashgabat, Merv and the Darvaza gas crater; July and August routinely exceed 40°C.

idp.text: Turkmenistan is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Vienna, 1968), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Vienna, 8 November 1968 (UNTS vol. 1042, p. 17)

driving.text: Turkmenistan is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Turkmenistan yet.

tips.text: Start the visa process 6–8 weeks before travel: the invitation letter alone takes 2–4 weeks to be approved by the State Migration Service, and applications can be refused at any stage without a reason given.

Tourist visas are tied to an accompanied itinerary. A licensed guide must accompany you outside Ashgabat. Only the transit visa allows unescorted travel, along a fixed route between named border points.
Do not photograph government buildings, the airport, military sites or police. Officers actively enforce this, and phones may be checked.

Overlanders relying on a transit visa between Iran and Uzbekistan should have a backup route (for example via the Caspian ferry or flying over) — transit-visa refusal rates are high and decisions arrive late.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Turkmenistan?
faq.answer: Yes — every nationality needs a visa, and for tourism it must be backed by a letter of invitation approved by the State Migration Service, arranged through a licensed Turkmen tour operator. There is no visa-free entry and no standard eVisa.

faq.question: How do I get a Turkmenistan letter of invitation?
faq.answer: Book with a licensed Turkmen tour operator, who submits your details to the State Migration Service. Approval typically takes 2–4 weeks and can be refused without explanation. With the approved letter you apply at an embassy, or collect the visa on arrival at Ashgabat airport.

faq.question: Can I get a Turkmenistan visa on arrival?
faq.answer: Only in a limited sense: travelers whose invitation letter has already been approved can have the visa issued on arrival at Ashgabat airport and certain land borders, paying the fee in US dollars cash. Without an approved invitation you will be refused boarding or entry.

faq.question: Is there a Turkmenistan transit visa without an invitation letter?
faq.answer: No. The transit visa, for up to 5 days per trip, also needs a letter of invitation sponsored by the State Migration Service, and you must enter and leave through the border crossings named on it. It is meant for overland crossings (typically between Iran and Uzbekistan) and is the most frequently refused Turkmen visa, so plan an alternative route.

faq.question: Can I travel independently in Turkmenistan?
faq.answer: Not on a tourist visa. An accredited guide must accompany you outside Ashgabat, and your itinerary is fixed in advance. Transit-visa holders may travel unescorted, but only along the route named on the visa and within its few days of validity.
